intro.title: Build typed GraphQL result helpers
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a set of helper functions to safely handle and type the results from a GraphQL API call. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generic types and type guards to create functions that check if a result is an error or contains valid data. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system and basic function definitions. By the end, you'll have reusable helpers that make your GraphQL integration more robust and type-safe.
intro.usecase: Typed GraphQL result helpers are essential for building robust data-driven frontends, such as admin dashboards and e-commerce platforms. For example, a dashboard displaying user analytics or a product catalog with filters relies on fetching complex, nested data from a GraphQL API. These helpers ensure that the data structure returned from the API matches the TypeScript types used in UI components, preventing runtime errors in tables, charts, or detail panels. By implementing them, developers can confidently manage data fetching in real-world applications, improving code reliability and developer experience during feature development and maintenance.
